title: Baby Bhakat, the civet cat
body: Bhakat is a three-month-old baby civet cat who lives with a human family in a thatched hut by a river in a small village in Assam. Its civet mother had built a nest in a very tall coconut tree, but one night the baby slipped and fell to the ground. Villagers took it to Dharini, who loves animals and, with his family, rescues and rehabilitates wild animals. Anjali, whom Bhakat calls Mama, feeds it before anyone else. Bhakat is nocturnal and arboreal: its large eyes help it see in the dark and its long tail helps it balance on branches. When the river flooded the house during the monsoon, snails climbed branches and walls to escape drowning, and Dharini picked snails for Bhakat. Bhakat says that by eating snails it stops them from overrunning gardens, since snails eat plants, and so it maintains the balance of life in nature. (Summary based on the story by Rommel Shunmugam in the unit.)
